clue.text: Maim swindler's accomplice, being hot stuff

parts.note: to scotch is an old word for wounding or disabling, as in scotching a snake
a bonnet is old slang for a con man's decoy or shill, who lures victims in

explanation.surface: Someone injures a con man's sidekick, and it turns out to be a sizzling affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are old-fashioned senses: SCOTCH meaning to wound, and BONNET for a cardsharp's stooge.
explanation.definitionFit: This pepper is among the fiercest chillies used in Caribbean cooking, so it is literally fiery food.

clue.text: Small hamper containing a vegetable

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: containing says the word for hamper holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to pinch is to constrict or restrict, so it can hamper

explanation.surface: A little wicker basket with a vegetable packed inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb, restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: This leafy green plant is a common garden vegetable eaten raw or cooked.

clue.text: Animal king a debut for composer describes

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the opus pair circles the next letters

parts.note: a composer's first catalogued work is Op. 1, opus one, written OP I
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch's beast is portrayed in a young composer's first work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' is used in its geometric sense, tracing a line round something, so OPI goes round KA.
explanation.definitionFit: This shy giraffe relative of the Congo forests is a mammal, so an animal.

clue.text: Robe that reveals bird's round buttocks

indicators.note: round says the bird goes around the buttocks

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, here the outer piece
ass is a slang word for the backside

explanation.surface: A garment that is cut so as to show off a plump bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's round' reads as the bird being round; the bird goes round the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: This long garment is the ankle-length robe worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: See 1 across
It's not very long after love letter

indicators.note: after places the tiny length behind the zero

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, written O
a micron is a millionth of a metre, a minute length

explanation.surface: Something brief follows a love note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love letter' looks like one phrase, but love gives O and 'letter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fifteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so a letter.

clue.text: Books on Germany found in famous cathedral

indicators.note: found in says the following pieces sit within the word for famous

parts.note: a name brand or name act is a famous one, so name can mean famous
OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
re means on or about, as in a letter heading
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Some German books turn up in a well-known cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous cathedral' looks like the definition, but 'famous' is NAME, the container.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gothic church on the Île de la Cité in Paris is one of the world's best-known cathedrals.

clue.text: A piece to play, zero volume, extending so long

indicators.note: extending says the goodbye is stretched by having the other pieces put inside it

parts.note: ta-ta is a casual way of saying goodbye, like so long
zero looks like the letter O
cc, cubic centimetres, is a unit of volume

explanation.surface: A musical item is played, silent at first, then dragged out at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' suggests duration but is TATA, goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a showy keyboard composition, typically for organ, so a musical piece to perform.

clue.text: Standard, forbidding one

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag carried on a pole
someone who bans or forbids things

explanation.definitionFit: A flag carried in procession is a standard; one who bans is literally a forbidder.

clue.text: Location of Hollywood idol in need of new material?

parts.note: Hollywood is in California, abbreviated Cal

indicators.note: in need of says the idol is lacking the letter for new

parts.note: an icon is an idolised figure

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star wonders where they could get some fresh cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In need of new' sounds like a call for something fresh; it says ICON is short of its N.
explanation.definitionFit: This plain-woven cotton cloth is a fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Ljungberg, say, has reason to get excited, rounding Manchester's No 1 to get Arsenal's fifth

indicators.note: rounding says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
excited letters are agitated and stirred up, so the word reason is rearranged
number one is the first letter of Manchester
fifth picks the fifth letter of Arsenal

explanation.surface: A Swedish footballer has cause to celebrate after a goal against Manchester, setting up Arsenal's fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of REASON as NORSEA has M put in to give NORSEMA. Freddie Ljungberg was a Swedish midfielder for Arsenal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a Scandinavian, and the word for a man of the North covers any Scandinavian.

clue.text: See 23
Beadle introducing people competing on buzzer

indicators.note: introducing puts the beadle first, ahead of the competitors

parts.note: Mr Bumble is the parish beadle in Dickens's Oliver Twist
a bee is a gathering of people competing, as in a spelling bee

explanation.surface: A TV presenter introduces contestants on a quiz with a buzzer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Jeremy Beadle the TV host; the beadle is Dickens's Bumble.
explanation.definitionFit: This furry insect buzzes as it flies, so it is a buzzer.

clue.text: All but in the clear over Batty Bernhardt's detailed self-introduction

indicators.note: in places the turned phrase inside the clear

parts.note: net means clear, as in clear profit after deductions

indicators.note: over in an across clue turns each of the two pieces backwards where it stands
detailed means having its tail cut off, losing the last letter

parts.note: batty means mad, and Sarah Bernhardt was the famous French actress
I'm is how one introduces oneself

explanation.surface: A dotty actress, telling all about herself, almost comes clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns MADSARA (MAD SARAH with its tail, the H, cut by 'detailed') into ARASDAM and I'M into MI; both go inside NET.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means almost exactly, a close approximation, just as all but means nearly.

clue.text: See 14
Reduce to nothing extra-terrestrial ring

parts.note: to annul is to cancel, make void
ET is the film alien, the abbreviation for extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: An alien's ring is wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry and architecture this term names a small ring or ring-shaped moulding.

clue.text: I won't cross the line to give the fellow a beating

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to give them a beating
a gent is a fellow, a gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stay in bounds when giving a man a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the thing itself: a line that touches a curve without crossing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this straight line meets a curve at one point without cutting through it.

clue.text: Panther's what's caught by man on time

parts.note: a bag is the haul a hunter or angler catches
he is the pronoun for a man
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A big cat is landed by a hunter in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the black panther who guides Mowgli in Kipling's The Jungle Book.

clue.text: How things get repeated up amongst the Tory backbenchers

indicators.note: up in a down clue says those letters read from the bottom
amongst says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Back-bench Conservatives echo the party line mechanically.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from memory by mechanical repetition, the way lessons or slogans are recited.

clue.text: City is as good in luminous appearance

indicators.note: in says the middle pieces go into the glow

parts.note: a glow is a luminous appearance

explanation.surface: A city looks every bit as fine when lit up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Scotland's largest city, on the River Clyde.

clue.text: Reddish-brown American band getting into line

indicators.note: getting into says the pieces go inside the line

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
US means American
a set is a band or group

explanation.surface: An American band gets into a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a reddish-brown colour, and this adjective means tinged with it.

clue.text: A cosmetic joke

parts.note: a means one
liner, as in eyeliner, is a cosmetic

explanation.surface: Make-up as a gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip delivered in a single sentence is a short joke.

clue.text: I can't find my way, but motorway has left ahead, 14 15

indicators.note: the motorway letter M gets the left letter L in front of it, so L shifts forward

parts.note: someone who can't find their way says they am lost, in the clue's first-person voice

explanation.surface: A lost driver finds the motorway turning is on the left ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motorway' names the M of AMLOST; L (left) moves ahead of it. The definition is 14 15, NEAR AS DAMMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-referenced idiom means very nearly, exactly what this word means.

clue.text: Horribly numb with heartbreak after the loss of a family man with Rolls

indicators.note: horribly suggests letters badly mangled and rearranged
after the loss of says one A is taken from heartbreak

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grieving family man is left horribly numb by heartbreak after a bereavement.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Families is a British card game of illustrated trades; the baker, with his bread rolls, is one card. 'Rolls' suggests the car.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the baker in the Happy Families card set, a family man whose trade is bread rolls.

clue.text: Feminine freedom fighter acquires rock in faraway country, the gossip

parts.note: a libber is a campaigner for liberation, as in women's lib

indicators.note: in places the Rock inside the country

parts.note: Tibet is the remote Himalayan land
Gib is short for Gibraltar, the Rock

explanation.surface: A feminist campaigner picks up a stone in Tibet and becomes a chatterbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acquires' is a link word here; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for a flighty, frivolous chatterer, a gossip.

clue.text: Scores in cricket competition, it's clear

definitions.meaning: a score is ..., so two scores are two lots of ...
the short-form cricket format of ... overs a side
perfect eyesight, measured as 20/20 vision, is clear sight

explanation.definitionFit: Two twenties make scores; the short cricket format and perfect eyesight share the same figures.
